recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit for FHIR-11169. Review FHIR-39458 separately if a distinct audit of the category/code split is desired; handle any broader V3 or THO terminology cleanup through the terminology governance path rather than a core DetectedIssue.category edit.
issue_request: FHIR-11169 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification CDS change request asking that DetectedIssue.category be carefully examined and cleaned up because the preferred V3-derived category value set included confusing duplicate late-start/late-end concepts and semantically misplaced PREVINEF.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-11169 was found. The Jira later comment links HL7/fhir pull request #3305, whose merge commit 065b66f62534babf9063f00a4ad89f7a865b9906 included commit 34181b9f2184a72b527d9f5b26c234c0c07669ed restricting the category value set and creating the separate DetectedIssue code value set.
additional_context: DetectedIssue is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/detectedissue files feed the current build. Related Applied issue FHIR-39458 split DetectedIssue.category from DetectedIssue.code; that same implementation path left the current category value set with only category-level v3-ActCode concepts. The old V3 terminology source still contains the detailed concepts named by FHIR-11169, but those concepts are no longer exposed through DetectedIssue.category.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current DetectedIssue.category binding points to a cleaned value set containing only FOOD, DRUG, ALGY, and DUPTHPY, while detailed detected-issue codes are in the separate DetectedIssue.code value set.
